utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Case number IT-97-25/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Savo Todovic and Mitar Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Can we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff. I represent the Prosecution today and I am accompanied by the case manager, Sebastian van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic and I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Savo Todovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Vladimir Domazet representing the accused, Mitar Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber today, the 21st of March, 2005 bids good afternoon to all those present, to the representatives of the Prosecution, the two advocates and the two accused who are present today. As you know, this is a Status Conference within the framework of Rule 65, according to which a Status Conference shall be convened within 120 days after the initial appearance. We have a new accused who has arrived in the meantime, and I'm going to ask Mr. Todovic to be kind enough to stand. Mr. Todovic. You may be seated, Mr. Rasevic, as we have already seen each other and I know you. So will you give me your name and your date of birth, please. THE ACCUSED TODOVIC: [Interpretation] My name is Savo Todovic. I was born on the 11th of December, 1952.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You are able to follow what I'm saying in your own language? THE ACCUSED TODOVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, you may be seated. THE ACCUSED TODOVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to briefly remind you of the procedure. First of all, the Prosecutor, on the 6th of January, 1997, issued an indictment against the three accused. At the time there was Milorad Krnojelac, Mr. Savo Todovic, and Mr. Mitar Rasevic. This indictment of the 6th of June, 1997 was confirmed by Judge Vohrah on the 17th of June 1997. Following that, the accused Krnojelac was transferred to the Tribunal in June 1998 and he was judged by Trial Chamber which rendered its judgement on the 15th of March, 2002 and following by the Appeals Chamber which also rendered its judgement on the 17th of September, 2003. In the meantime, the accused, Mitar Rasevic, came to the Tribunal and the indictment with regard to him was modified on the 12th of May, 2004. On the other hand, regarding the accused Todovic, the indictment of the 6th of June, 1997 is the legal basis for the current proceedings. Regarding this indictment of the 6th of June, 1997, the Prosecution has filed a motion on the 14th of March, 2005 requesting the Chamber to rule on a motion of the Defence for the accused Todovic, which was filed on the 10th of March, 2005. Consequently, the Chamber needs to rule and I will shortly render a decision ordering the Prosecution to amend the indictment of June 1997 so that that indictment may be in conformity with the indictment for Mr. Rasevic which was modified or amended in May, 2004. In the meantime, the Prosecution has seized the Tribunal of a request based on Rule 11 bis to have this case transferred to a national jurisdiction and a request was filed on the 1st of November, 2004 for the Todovic case, and on the 4th of November, 2004 for the Rasevic case. Today, I don't know where we stand with respect to that request. The Chamber, resided by Judge Orie needs to render a decision with respect to the possible transfer of this case to a national jurisdiction. I don't know what is the position of the accused, whether they are in favour or not, I don't know, but perhaps the Defence counsel will be able to inform me about that in a moment. Regarding the 11 bis motion, it will be up to the Chamber formed for that purpose to rule regarding that matter. Therefore, in brief, for the moment, we have two outstanding motions, the motion of the accused Todovic with respect to an error in form of the indictment, and the motion of the 14th of March, 2005 requesting the Chamber to rule on the motion of the Defence for Mr. Todovic. Independently of these matters, during the Status Conference held in November, I asked the Prosecution to provide me with the pre-trial brief, because at that time, in November, I thought that the case was taking too much time and that the Chamber should be informed about it. The Prosecution, by motion, has asked for this delay to be extended to the 1st of April. I granted that request. But with the arrival of the accused Todovic, a similar question arises, that is, with respect to the pre-trial brief to the extent to which the accused Todovic is entitled to be informed in accordance with Rule 66(A) and (I) and with Rule 68 with the supporting material and the brief. However, as we now have two accused, I assume that the case will be delayed to some extent. Could the Prosecution first of all, tell me whether Judge Orie's Chamber has given a date regarding the consideration of 11 bis motions and what are the intentions of the Prosecution as we now have the two accused present here and whether this case will be tried here; if so, the two accused need to be tried simultaneously or in their own country. So could the Prosecution provide me with this information?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Trial Chamber has not yet scheduled this case as there is not yet a hearing scheduled. This is probably due to the fact that I actually had requested together with the Defence not to have this hearing because we were having negotiations. In open session, I don't want to address these negotiations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You would like us to go into private session? Mr. Registrar, shall we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In open session, as the Pre-Trial Judge, I need to tell the Prosecution that regardless of all the other procedures that are underway, that they need to communicate to the Defence of Mr. Todovic the supporting material and Rule 66(A) and Rule 68. Can the Prosecution inform me that these legal obligations have been fulfilled to the letter?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have disclosed the supporting material within the 30 days; that's done. And the other disclosure is an ongoing process and we will, of course, fulfill our obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Regarding the disclosure of material, are there any problems on the side of the Defence counsel? Is everything running smoothly, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can confirm that everything is ongoing. We have received further disclosure, the documents that were supportive for the indictment and that these are six binders of documents and I can confirm that I received them and it's now on the Defence to discuss these issues with the detainees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. I now need to ask the accused to comment on the conditions of detention and their state of health. Mr. Rasevic, will you stand, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Mr. Rasevic, can you tell me whether you have anything to say about conditions of detention, are they still good? THE ACCUSED RASEVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you for asking, Your Honour. The conditions of detention are still good. I have absolutely no remarks or comments to make. My health is good. I am grappling with certain financial problems. The only thing that is that this is going on for so long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I take note of that. THE ACCUSED RASEVIC: [Interpretation] I have nothing more to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Rasevic. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Todovic, will you stand, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Todovic, as you have just arrived, I need to draw your attention to a few of the rules of procedure with respect to conditions of detention. Rule 84 stays that all detainees may, at any time, file a request or a complaint to the commander of the Detention Unit or his representative. If you are not satisfied with the response of the Detention Unit commander, you can file a complaint in writing which will be forwarded to the Registrar of this Tribunal and then to the President of the Tribunal. Also, according to Rule 86, you have the ability to communicate freely with the inspection authority, so a Judge may, should there be a problem, come to see you in the prison to address all problems linked to your detention. Pursuant to Rule 87, when you file a complaint, that complaint will be treated confidentially and according to Rule 88, when you file a complaint, they must be dealt with as soon as possible. Therefore, in more -- most general terms, the way in which -- should you have any problems in the Detention Unit, address them through a complaint addressed to the Registrar, the commander of the prison, or the Pre-Trial Judge. Regardless of this matter, I need to ask you, even though you arrived only recently, have you encountered any difficulties? If so, let me know. Do you have anything to tell me regarding your conditions of detention? THE ACCUSED TODOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the conditions of detention are perfectly correct at the highest level. The personnel are fair. My condition -- health conditions are good so that I have nothing further to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Todovic. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that we will shortly have a clear situation whether this case will be tried here or in the country of origin of the two accused, as it is stipulated that the accused Rasevic has been here for sometime and as he has just said, it seems a long time for him. The Prosecution have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I have two issues, and it's all about timing. First of all, in our recent motion from 14 March, we have indicated in paragraph 3 that an interview is scheduled with the accused Todovic and it was indeed scheduled for this week. Only this morning, before the hearing, Mr. Lazarevic informed me that it cannot take place this week because Mr. Todovic wants to consider first the material in more details. Therefore, because of the Easter break, this interview can only take place mid-April. That means what we can do is we can still file the amended indictment at the last day of April. I think that's workable for us after having heard him to adjust the indictment, but the pre-trial brief, that line, is the 1st of April and the -- we would request to -- the Prosecution requests to vacate this deadline because I think the pre-trial brief should be a joint pre-trial brief for both accused and it can actually only be done when their proceedings are in the same stage, that means after the amendment of the indictment, Mr. Lazarevic, for the Defence, can again attack this indictment and after this is dealt with, I would think it's probably mid-June that we can file a pre-trial brief for both. Therefore, I'd suggest to set these deadlines for the amendment of the indictment, the last day of April and for the pre-trial brief, the 15th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Prosecution has just informed me that, on the one hand, in the Prosecution's opinion, given the issue of amending the indictment, the indictment could only be amended about the 15th of June. And it's possible for the accused Todovic to contested the indictment; however, if the case is to be tried here, it's necessary to have one indictment, an identical indictment for both accused, and if the case is to be referred to the country of origin, in that case, it is also necessary for the indictment to be the same one. There is a matter that has to be dealt with, but in my opinion, this should not take too much time. Because as the Appeals Chamber has ruled in the Krnojelac affair, an indictment from May that concerns Mr. Rasevic has taken these changes into consideration. So as far as Mr. Todovic is concerned, the situation should be similar as far as this indictment is concerned and the legal conclusions drawn by the Appeals Chamber in the Krnojelac case. That's not the difficulty. The only difficulty that remains is the time that the parties need to reach or not to reach an agreement, that's another issue and also the Chamber presided by Judge Orie must rapidly be informed of the agreements or disagreements between the parties so that they can render their decision pursuant to Rule 11 bis. Whatever the case may be, it is now March. I'll have four months to see you again, if necessary, that brings us to April, May, June, July, the beginning of July. So if nothing advances, if nothing progresses, we'll see each other again at the beginning of July for a Status Conference, and I hope that that will be the last one because this case is starting to take too much time and I think that Mr. Domazet is of the same opinion. Very well, are there any other issues that either of the parties would like to raise, the Prosecution, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Nothing arises, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I thank you all, and as I have said, we have now dealt with all the items on the agenda for this Status Conference. And if necessary, we will see each other at the beginning of July for another Status Conference. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
